I've watched War of the Worlds and finished Game of Thrones and I'm wondering if it is worth buying and reading the books. A friend told me it is very worth it, as it goes in depth much more, but I feel like knowing what will happen kind of ruins the idea for me.

What are your guys' thoughts on reading afterwards? Not worth it? A must-do?
Are reading the books after watching a series/movie worth it? Any examples of why or why not?

For me the beauty of reading fiction is to give my imagination the freedom to picture the individuals and their surroundings/environments. This is even more pronounced for fantasy world novels. That's why I never read the book if I saw the movie first.

I did it with a Song of Ice and Fire and Blade Runner. Sometimes a movie/show just clicks with you that when you find out there's a book (or multiple books) behind it, just makes you want to pick it up and give it a go.
Did you find yourself upset knowing what happens in the book anyway?
Nope. I go in knowing it's likely going to be a slightly different story, as all movie/show adaptations are.

The best example I have of the book being better than the movie, is The Green Mile, written by Stephen King. The movie, while also great, completely leaves out Mr. Jingles, the mouse. I really felt that the movie missed something by leaving that story line out.

With regards to the George RR Martin books. I think you should read them. There's a lot they didn't cover in the TV series. Besides, they're so action packed that I don't think you will remember every detail of the TV series as you read through them.
Thank you for your suggestion and input, I really enjoy Stephen King's novels as well!

The Green Mile is an excellet suggestion.

Yes, the movie is great and some people might argue that you can't compare the two mediums, but the book left me feeling way more emotionally connected to the characters than the movie, especially the head guard.

Generally, I would say yes. Books tend to be a lot more detailed than TV shows and films, so if you find that you really like a show and want to immerse yourself more in its world, the book(s) is usually a good way to do that.

For War of the Worlds especially I would say yes, both because the book is a lot better and because it isn't even a very long book, so it's easy to pick up. A Song of Ice and Fire is admittedly a big commitment, but worth it if you're willing.

How many people do you know only watch something they enjoyed only once because they know what happens? Are you never going to rewatch scenes Game of Thrones? If so, then you probably don't want to read.

Usually when books and comics are adapted into movies and shows, no matter how good they are, they are going to lose details due to time limits and other constraints. Sub-plots and characters disappear. Some warp and change into something new (for better or worse).

If you loved the work made off of the originals, rarely is it a misstep to go back and see what the originals were all about. With new details, the results are going to feel different even if you know what's coming for the main plot. Heck, with many larger works with there are going to be bunch of other things you will not see coming. Little things that build up. Rarely is it the other way around.

The only time this doesn't work is when it comes to adaptions that are heavily modernized and/or are so damned different from the original you wonder why they even kept the same title.
I can't speak about Game of Thrones, but Wells' War of the Worlds still has never been made faithfully into a movie, and is a damn great book in its own right.

I would venture that it's always worth it.

Books (when they are the source material) tend to be much better than their film counterparts. There are always exceptions, of course, but I'm sure that they are few and far between. Plus books and their movie counterparts are usually different in many ways. You can't cram a whole novel into a movie, so lots of material often gets cut, as well as lots getting changed for whatever reasons.

As for the end being spoiled. There is more to a book than just the ending.

I've spent 4 years working in the Northern Ontario wilderness during the height of bug season, regarded as on-par much the worst in world. Some areas further north will more commonly have the most extreme swarms of mosquitoes, but those certainly happen with the proper conditions there. The black flies are unreal, and No-see-um swarms are common, along with horse/deer/whatever you wanna call them flies during the heat.

But since you asked specifically about mosquitoes, here is how you do it:

-Typical back yard nuisance level

DEET works. The higher the concentration, the better. For your typical back yard minor nuisance amount of mosquitoes 40% is still better than the weaker stuff, just apply to your hands and spread it around your sensitive spots, and on top of any tight fitting clothes, or anywhere the clothes will be pulled tight to your skin.

Alternately, I prefer to wear loose long sleeved dress shirt, and loose pants. The loose sleeves keep them from biting, and the collar can be raised to protect your neck. A little DEET on the collar can help prevent them from flying down, but in my opinion using DEET as infrequently as possible is the best option for someone who has daily bug exposure, you'll get used to them especially if your clothes help protect you.

Some swear by citronella oil. I do not think it helps very much beyond a mild nuisance.

Hang around someone they like more. Sometimes they just seem to prefer a certain person, god bless these bug magnets

-Bug apocalypse level, these still work with the lower amounts of insects:

A bug shirt (something like this http://img.diytrade.com/cdimg/1068493/11495206/0/1277452872/Outdoor_bug_shirt.jpg) can be very nice if you can stand the heat inside it. It should be small enough that no-see-ums cannot crawl through the mesh, and you must be weary of it being tight against your skin or the mosquitoes will bite right through. I cannot stand these but I still always kept one on me so I could relax while waiting for a pick-up after all the work is done, or if I absolutely need a break from the swarm. Warning: if blacks flies are around make sure all entrances are sealed or they will crawl into it and feast on your pink flesh.

Wearing a darker colour on your legs, and white on your torso will cause most biting insects to swarm your legs more than your upper body. This will make your DEET more effective on your upper body as less bugs will be rubbing it off you as they attempt to land on your skin/clothes. Black and blue are a biting insects favorite colours and wearing these is inviting them to land and move around these colours.

High DEET cream is better than spray on for me. Its not sold in many areas but Watkin's cream has worked amazingly for me, requiring few applications, and having less aerosol poison projecting around my orifices.

KEEP MOVING. If your job needs you to move, move quickly. You can out move the majority of your following swarm

Smoking cigarettes when your hands are busy. You can still blow smoke on the bastards and they don't like that. Also in this is the classic standing in the smoke of your campfire, although this seems to only discourage them for a few moments after you leave the smoke cloud.

Some people rub their bodies in various vegetable oils, I have never seen this personally but some greasy wilderness hippies swear by it.

Also, do not let mosquitoes into your sealed living enclosures. They wait and lurk and eat you as you sleep.
